$comment: Wiring rules for the Velxio agent, one entry per component family or id. This is the only hand-maintained part of the agent catalog: scripts/generate-agent-catalog.mjs merges it with frontend/public/components-metadata.json (ids, properties, defaults), scripts/agent-pins.json (measured pin names) and the live simulation registry into backend/app/agent/catalog.json + frontend/src/agent/catalog.json. Vocabulary: class (grouping used for wording), placeable, why (when not), pinPatterns (regex -> signal rules, expanded by the generator), signal {pin: {cap, dir, optional, severity}}, power {pin: supply|ground}, bus [{type, pins, when?}], selfShortPairs (pins that must not share a net), internalPairs (pins joined inside the part), tracePairs (pass-through when active), seriesResistor {pins, min, each?}, gateResistor {pins, min}, externalDriver {pins, why, via}, powerOut (pins that ARE a supply rail), interactions (press|pot|switch|rotary|stimulus), stimulusKeys (sensor-model keys the browser can drive), rotary {role: pin}, addressProperty (I2C address the user can change), libraries (headers a sketch may include), notes (the wiring paragraph shown to the model). cap values: gpio, analog, pwm, i2c-sda, i2c-scl, spi-sck, spi-mosi, spi-miso, uart-tx, uart-rx.

spec.notes: Two-terminal resistor. `value` in ohms (100..1e7). In series with an LED use 220-1000; as a pull-up/pull-down 1k-100k; as a base resistor 1k-10k.
Ceramic capacitor. Decoupling between a supply and GND; a timing capacitor on a GPIO must be charged through a resistor.
Electrolytic capacitor: `+` to the higher potential, `−` to GND. Never reverse it.
Inductor. A GPIO cannot drive one directly — use a transistor with a flyback diode.
Diode: anode (A) toward the driving side, cathode (C, the stripe) toward the load/rail. Flyback diodes go across inductive loads, reverse-biased.
NPN transistor: E to GND, load between +V and C, B driven through a base resistor (1k-10k) from a GPIO. That is how a GPIO switches anything bigger than an LED.
PNP transistor: E to +V, load between C and GND, B to GND through a resistor to switch it on (a GPIO drives it LOW).
MOSFET: S to GND (N-channel), load between +V and D, G through a 10-220 ohm gate resistor, plus a 10k pull-down from G to S so it cannot float on.
Op-amp (the model has no supply pins): OUT swings between the rails. No feedback network is required, but no input may float.
Optocoupler: drive AN through a 220-1k resistor (CAT to GND) and use COL/EMIT as the isolated switch on the other side.
Linear regulator: VIN from an unregulated supply, VOUT is the regulated rail for the rest of the circuit. Never wire VOUT (or VIN) to a GPIO.
Adjustable regulator: VIN from the supply, ADJ sets the output, VOUT is the regulated rail. Never wire VOUT to a GPIO.
Battery: `+` is the supply rail, `−` the ground. Use it for loads a GPIO cannot drive (motors, relays, servos) and join the grounds.
Logic gate: inputs A..D must be driven by GPIOs (or another output), Y is the output. The model has no power pins — never leave an input floating.
Edge-triggered flip-flop: CLK and D/J/K/T are inputs, Q/Qbar outputs. Drive CLK from a GPIO and expect one state change per rising edge.
74HC logic IC: VCC to 5V, GND to GND, and an unused input must never float — tie it to a rail or drive it. Outputs (nY) can drive a GPIO input, or an LED through a series resistor.
E-paper over SPI (hardware SCK=13, MOSI=11 on the Uno; CS/DC/RST on free GPIOs). BUSY is an output from the panel. A full refresh takes seconds.
Character LCD in 4-bit parallel mode: RS, E and D4-D7 (6 GPIOs), VDD=5V, VSS=GND, K=GND (backlight cathode), V0 to a 10k contrast pot. Use the LiquidCrystal library; wire D0-D3 only for 8-bit mode.
I2C character LCD backpack: VCC=5V, GND, SDA=A4, SCL=A5 (Uno), address 0x27/0x3F. Construct LiquidCrystal_I2C with that address.

led.notes: LED: A=anode (long leg), C=cathode. Always in series with a 220-1000 ohm resistor; use a PWM pin (3,5,6,9,10,11) for brightness.

rgb-led.notes: RGB LED with a common cathode (COM to GND): R/G/B are three separate LEDs, each needing its own 150-330 ohm resistor. PWM each channel to mix colours.

led-bar-graph.notes: 10-segment bar graph: C1..C10 are the cathodes (GND), A1..A10 the anodes, each needing its own series resistor.

neopixel.notes: WS2812 strip: 5V, GND, data into DIN (a 300-500 ohm series resistor and a large electrolytic across the supply are good practice). Drive it with Adafruit_NeoPixel; never power a long strip from the Uno's 5V pin.

neopixel-matrix.notes: WS2812 matrix: VCC=5V, GND, DIN from a GPIO through a series resistor; DOUT chains on to the next panel.

led-ring.notes: WS2812 ring: 5V, GND, DIN from a GPIO. Set the pixel-count property to the ring size.

7segment.notes: 7-segment display: every segment (A-G, DP) needs its own 220-470 ohm resistor, and the common pin (COM.1/COM.2, or CLN/COM on the 4-digit module) goes to GND. With digits>1 multiplex DIG1..DIG4 and keep the refresh fast.

buzzer.notes: Piezo buzzer: pin 1 to GND, pin 2 to a GPIO. Drive it with tone() (or analogWrite for volume on a PWM pin).

pushbutton.notes: Momentary pushbutton. It has TWO contacts and each contact has two legs joined inside the part: contact 1 = 1.l + 1.r, contact 2 = 2.l + 2.r; pressing closes contact 1 to contact 2. Wire the GPIO to ONE contact and GND to the OTHER (e.g. GPIO to 1.l, GND to 2.l) and read it with pinMode(pin, INPUT_PULLUP) - it reads LOW while pressed. GPIO on 1.l with GND on 1.r is both legs of the SAME contact: a dead short that ties the pin to GND and never switches.

pushbutton-6mm.notes: Panel-mount pushbutton — same contacts as the standard one: contact 1 = 1.l + 1.r, contact 2 = 2.l + 2.r (legs of one contact are joined inside). GPIO (INPUT_PULLUP) on one contact and GND on the OTHER (GPIO to 1.l, GND to 2.l); GPIO on 1.l with GND on 1.r is the same contact, a dead short.

slide-switch.notes: SPDT slide switch: 2 is the common, 1 and 3 the throws. Common to a GPIO (INPUT_PULLUP), one throw to GND — or use both throws as a selector. The `value` property is the resting position.

tilt-switch.notes: Tilt sensor module: OUT changes level when tilted. Read it with INPUT_PULLUP (check the module's polarity).

dip-switch-8.notes: 8-way DIP switch: each Na-Nb pair is an independent SPST switch. Na to a GPIO with INPUT_PULLUP, Nb to GND is the usual wiring.

membrane-keypad.notes: 4x4 matrix keypad: R1-R4 rows, C1-C4 columns (8 GPIOs). Scan the rows and read the columns with INPUT_PULLUP. It cannot be auto-stimulated in the browser.

ky-040.notes: Rotary encoder with a push button: CLK/DT are the quadrature outputs (pull-ups are on the module), SW is the shaft button. Read CLK in an interrupt and SW with INPUT_PULLUP.

rotary-dialer.notes: Pulse-dial telephone dial: PULSE gives one pulse per digit, DIAL marks that a digit is being dialled. Count pulses in an interrupt.

potentiometer.notes: Potentiometer: VCC=5V, GND=GND, SIG to an analog pin (A0-A5). Read it with analogRead — the wiper is a voltage divider, so it cannot be read as a digital pin.

slide-potentiometer.notes: Slide potentiometer: the same three terminals as a rotary pot (VCC, GND, SIG to an analog pin).

analog-joystick.notes: Analog joystick: VERT/HORZ to two analog pins, SEL is a push button (INPUT_PULLUP to GND). Use the pot interaction with a pin name to drive one axis.

dht22.notes: DHT22 temperature/humidity: VCC=5V, GND, SDA to any GPIO with a 10k pull-up to 5V, read at most every 2 s with the DHT library. The NC pin is unused.

hc-sr04.notes: HC-SR04 ultrasonic: TRIG gets a 10 us pulse from a GPIO, ECHO returns a pulse whose width is the distance (pulseIn; cm = width / 58).

pir-motion-sensor.notes: PIR motion module: OUT goes HIGH while motion is detected. Give it a second to settle after power-up.

photoresistor-sensor.notes: LDR module: AO is an analog light level (A0-A5), DO is a comparator output whose threshold comes from its trimpot.

photodiode.notes: Photodiode: reverse-biased (C toward the higher potential) it produces a small photocurrent — amplify it, or use an LDR module.

ntc-temperature-sensor.notes: NTC thermistor module: OUT to an analog pin; the voltage tracks temperature.

heart-beat-sensor.notes: Pulse sensor: OUT is an analog waveform, one peak per heartbeat. Threshold it in software to count beats per minute.

flame-sensor.notes: Flame sensor: AOUT is the analog intensity, DOUT a threshold output (usually active LOW).

gas-sensor.notes: Gas sensor: AOUT is the analog level, DOUT trips at the trimpot threshold. It needs a warm-up before readings settle.

big-sound-sensor.notes: Sound sensor (big): AOUT is the audio envelope, DOUT a threshold output. Sample AOUT with analogRead.

small-sound-sensor.notes: Sound sensor (small): the same pins as the big one, lower gain.

ir-receiver.notes: IR receiver module: DAT to any GPIO (the carrier is already demodulated). Decode with the IRremote library.

ir-remote.notes: IR remote handset: no wires — place it next to an IR receiver and stimulate the RECEIVER with address/command to send a frame.

bmp280.notes: BMP280 barometer over I2C: VCC=5V (module) or 3.3V, GND, SDA=A4, SCL=A5, address 0x76/0x77 (SDO picks it).

mpu6050.notes: MPU6050 IMU over I2C: VCC=5V (module), GND, SDA=A4, SCL=A5, address 0x68/0x69 (AD0 picks it). INT is optional.

ds1307.notes: DS1307 RTC over I2C at 0x68: 5V, GND, SDA=A4, SCL=A5. SQW can clock an interrupt pin. Set the time with RTClib's adjust().

ds3231.notes: DS3231 RTC over I2C at 0x68: VCC=5V, GND, SDA=A4, SCL=A5. It also reports temperature.

hx711.notes: HX711 load-cell amplifier: DT is the data output, SCK is clocked by the GPIO (HX711 library). Decode its own protocol — there is no sensor knob for it in the browser.

gps-neo6m.notes: NEO-6M GPS: TX to a GPIO used as SoftwareSerial RX (RX to a GPIO used as TX if you send commands). 9600 baud NMEA.

ssd1306.notes: SSD1306 128x64 OLED. I2C mode: CLK=SCL (A5), DATA=SDA (A4), the 3V3/VIN pin to a supply, address 0x3C. SPI mode uses CS/DC/RST instead — pick one mode and wire it completely.

ssd1306-i2c-4pin.notes: 4-pin I2C OLED (VCC, GND, SDA=A4, SCL=A5), address 0x3C — the easiest display to add to a project.

ili9341.notes: ILI9341 TFT over SPI: SCK=13, MOSI=11, CS/DC/RST on free GPIOs, MISO optional, LED (backlight) to 5V or a PWM pin. 3.3V logic — level-shift if you power it from 5V.

microsd-card.notes: microSD over SPI: SCK=13, DI=MOSI=11, DO=MISO=12, CS on GPIO 10 (the SD library default) or another pin. 3.3V supply and logic.

power-supply.notes: Bench supply: GND is the ground rail, SIG is the regulated output (set its voltage with the property). Use it instead of the Uno's 5V pin for anything that draws real current.

signal-generator.notes: Signal generator: GND plus a SIG output you can configure (waveform, frequency, amplitude). Feed it into a GPIO (or a load with a safe amplitude).

externalDriver.why: a relay coil draws far more current than a GPIO can source and kicks back when it switches off

relay.notes: Relay: COIL+/COIL- is the coil — drive it through a transistor (with a flyback diode), never straight from a GPIO. COM/NO/NC are the isolated contacts that switch your load.

externalDriver.why: a relay coil draws more current than a GPIO can source and needs a flyback diode

ks2e-m-dc5.notes: Two-pole relay: COIL1/COIL2 is the coil (drive it through a transistor); P1 with NO1/NC1 and P2 with NO2/NC2 are the two isolated poles.

motor-driver-l293d.notes: L293D dual H-bridge: VCC1=5V logic, VCC2=motor supply, the GND pins to GND. IN1-4 choose the direction, EN1/EN2 take PWM for speed, OUT1-4 go to the motors.

externalDriver.why: the stepper coils are driven by the A4988's own H-bridges, not by the board

a4988.notes: A4988 stepper driver: VDD=5V logic, VMOT=motor supply (with a 100uF capacitor across it), the GND pins to GND, STEP/DIR from GPIOs, ENABLE optional, MS1-3 set microstepping, 1A/1B/2A/2B to the stepper coils.

externalDriver.why: a stepper coil cannot be driven from a GPIO; it needs a driver (A4988 or L293D)

stepper-motor.notes: Bipolar stepper: A+/A-/B+/B- are the two coils. They go to a driver, never to the board.

externalDriver.why: stepper coils need H-bridge drivers, not GPIOs

biaxial-stepper.notes: Two-phase stepper with two coils per phase: every coil pair goes to a driver channel.

servo.notes: Hobby servo: PWM (the signal) on a PWM-capable pin (3,5,6,9,10,11), V+ and GND to a 5V supply that can deliver the stall current. Servo.h disables analogWrite on pins 9 and 10. Expect ~50 Hz pulses.

junction.why: a junction merges wires and has no pins to reason about; express nets with direct wires instead

breadboard.why: prototyping boards are wiring aids: their rows are nets, not part pins, and the analysis works on direct wires

breadboard-mini.why: same as the full breadboard — the agent wires parts directly

arduino-uno.notes: Placeable as an extra MCU board: it lands on the canvas as a second, independently wired Arduino Uno (multi-board). The project's primary build target remains the `board` field; this instance is a wired companion board.

arduino-nano.notes: Placeable as an extra MCU board: it lands on the canvas as a second, independently wired Arduino Nano (multi-board). The project's primary build target remains the `board` field.

arduino-mega.notes: Placeable as an extra MCU board: it lands on the canvas as a second, independently wired Arduino Mega (multi-board). The project's primary build target remains the `board` field.

franzininho.why: only the Arduino Uno is supported as a build target right now
